text:
maria: Hey — running into Cloudflare Workers runtime errors when importing the JS SDK in our worker bundle. Error is `Uncaught TypeError: require is not a function` and also a complaint about missing 'fs' / 'Buffer'. Published build works in Node but blows up on deploy to Workers. Any recommended pattern for shipping one package that works for Node + CF workers? :thinking:

samir: Can you paste the import you’re using and the error stack? Is your bundle targeting 'browser' in esbuild?

maria: Import is just `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference-js'` in an ESM worker. Bundled with esbuild via wrangler: `esbuild({ platform: 'browser', format: 'esm' })`. Error stack (deploy log):
```
TypeError: require is not a function
    at Object.<anonymous> (dist/index.cjs.js:1:12)
    at __webpack_require__ (bootstrap:19)
    ...
```
Also runtime: `ReferenceError: Buffer is not defined` when the library tries to decode a base64 artifact.

kevin: Classic ESM/CJS interop + node builtin bleed. If your published package still has a CJS entrypoint or imports node-only shims (fs, path, Buffer), the worker bundle might try to include them. Two common options: 1) Conditional exports + dual builds (import vs require fields) so bundlers pick the right file, or 2) ship a separate lightweight edge entrypoint (e.g. `@redwood/inference-js/edge`) that contains only web-compatible code.

jena: We already considered conditional exports but bundlers like vite/webpack/esbuild sometimes pick the wrong entry depending on resolution logic. For CF Workers I prefer an explicit `/edge` entry to avoid surprises. That edge package should avoid `node:buffer` and any sync fs usage and instead use web crypto and Uint8Arrays.

samir: Quick workaround: lazy-load node-only modules behind a `if (typeof process !== 'undefined' && process.versions?.node)` guard so the import never gets resolved in the browser bundle. But note: static bundlers may still include the code unless you use dynamic import inside the guard: `if (isNode) { await import('./node-utils.cjs') }`. That keeps Node-only bits out of the edge build.

maria: Good point. Are there recommended package.json fields to guide bundlers? I saw examples using `exports` with `import`/`require` and `browser` condition. Any snippets?

kevin: Example we’ve used:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs",
    "browser": "./dist/index.edge.mjs"
  },
  "./edge": {
    "import": "./dist/index.edge.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.edge.cjs"
  }
}
```
Put edge-specific small bundle at `./dist/index.edge.mjs`. Bundlers that respect `browser`/`import` should pick the right file; otherwise consumers can explicitly import `@redwood/inference-js/edge` to be safe.

jena: Also add a tiny README snippet for Workers + Vite/Wrangler configs. For esbuild via wrangler: ensure `platform: 'browser'` and `inject` or `define` for globals. Example alias to polyfill Buffer: in vite use `resolve.alias: { buffer: 'buffer' }` and `optimizeDeps.include: ['buffer']` — but that will make bundle bigger. I'd rather avoid Buffer polyfills entirely and change SDK code to use `globalThis.atob`/`btoa` or `crypto.subtle` where possible.

samir: For base64 decode on edge you can do: `const bytes = Uint8Array.from(atob(b64), c => c.charCodeAt(0))` — no Buffer needed. For HMAC / signing use Web Crypto: `crypto.subtle.importKey` + `sign` instead of `crypto.createHmac` from node.

maria: What about typings? Our customers are complaining that `types` resolution breaks when we have multiple entrypoints. TypeScript consumers want correct d.ts for both CJS and ESM entrypoints.

kevin: Keep a single `index.d.ts` in dist that is compatible with both. In package.json: `types: './dist/index.d.ts'`. If you publish an `/edge` entrypoint, add a small `index.edge.d.ts` and include a `types` key in `exports` via the `types` condition? (TypeScript doesn't read conditional exports for types reliably). Easiest is: keep top-level `types` that covers both, and include `/// <reference types=\"node\" />` guarded in the node-only declarations so edge consumers aren’t forced to have node types. Or split declarations into `index.d.ts` and `index.edge.d.ts` and document which to import.

jena: Another angle: publish two packages: `@redwood/inference` and `@redwood/inference-edge`. Fewer surprises for users, and we can optimize the edge package for size/compatibility. Downsides: maintenance overhead & duplicated docs. But it’s clearer for platform teams.

maria: OK. Also running into a retry problem: the SDK automatically retries on 5xx responses and CF Worker fetch seems to sometimes return an opaque 520 that then causes a retry and duplicate side effects in our backend. Any CX for configuring retries from the worker?

samir: SDK should allow passing a `retry: { retries: 0 }` in options or a `shouldRetry` hook where you can implement idempotency checks. For Workers specifically, we should expose `fetchOptions` passthrough so caller can set `keepalive` or custom headers (e.g., `Idempotency-Key`). We should also document that retries are only safe for idempotent routes.

kevin: Agreed — we'll add `client = new Redwood({ retry: { retries: 2, factor: 2 }, idempotencyHeader: 'x-idempotency-key' })` and have SDK add the header automatically if provided. For Workers, docs should recommend generating a UUID per logical operation.

edge-ci-bot: Deploy failed for branch feature/worker-sdk on wrangler publish — see log: `Error: failed to bundle: Could not resolve \"fs\" from \"node_modules/@redwood/inference-js/dist/index.cjs.js\"` (build at 2026-03-22T14:32:18Z).

maria: Thanks. Action items: 1) Kevin: prototype conditional exports + edge entrypoint PR, 2) Samir: add lazy-dynamic import guards in SDK for node-only code paths, 3) Jena: write docs + recommended wrangler/esbuild config and a short note about retries/idempotency. I’ll try the `@redwood/inference-js/edge` import as a short-term fix.

kevin: I'll open a draft PR with dist/index.edge.mjs + package.json exports snippet and a tiny README. Will set types: './dist/index.d.ts' and include an `index.edge.d.ts` if needed.

samir: I’ll add a test case in CI that runs a minimal worker bundle against the edge entrypoint to catch regressions (esbuild with platform: 'browser').

jena: I’ll add doc examples: esbuild config, vite config, wrangler.toml tips, and an FAQ about Buffer/crypto polyfills.

maria: Great — thanks everyone :thumbsup: If anyone hits this while I’m out, ping here and I’ll follow up on the PR comments.
